Cowboy Pasta Salad

Jump to RecipePrintRate
By: Joanna Cismaru •Last Updated: 8/11/26 2 Comments

Instaread

This Cowboy Pasta Salad has seasoned ground beef, crispy bacon, charred corn, black beans, sharp cheddar, and cherry tomatoes all tossed in a smoky barbecue mayo dressing with a kick of lime and chili powder. It feeds 10 people, it travels well, and it’s the kind of dish that disappears at a potluck before you even get a chance to serve yourself.

Every potluck has that one dish everyone crowds around. This is that dish.

Cowboy pasta salad is essentially a Tex-Mex cookout in a bowl. Seasoned ground beef, crispy bacon, charred corn, black beans, sharp cheddar, jalapeño, cherry tomatoes, and rotini pasta all brought together by a smoky barbecue mayo dressing that has absolutely no business being as good as it is. It feeds 10 people comfortably, it gets better as it sits, and it’s the kind of recipe that people ask you about before they’ve finished their first serving.

It also happens to be a complete meal on its own which makes it one of the more useful recipes in the summer rotation. Bring it to a cookout, serve it alongside grilled chicken, or eat it straight from the bowl standing at the open fridge. All valid options.

Why You’ll Love My Cowboy Pasta Salad

  • Start with the dressing. Mayo and sour cream give you the creamy base. Barbecue sauce brings the smoke. Lime juice cuts through so none of it sits heavy. Then chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika show up and the whole thing tastes like it was built for this exact salad. It was.
  • Char the corn. Don’t skip this part. A dry skillet, high heat, corn blistering and browning in spots, that’s where a good chunk of the cookout flavor actually comes from. It costs you 5 minutes. Corn straight from the bag into the bowl just doesn’t taste the same, not even close.
  • Rinse the pasta. Cold water stops the cooking and washes off the starch clinging to the surface, the stuff that turns a cold pasta salad into a gluey mess if you skip this. Non negotiable for any pasta salad going into the fridge.
  • And then there’s the ground beef, which sounds strange in a pasta salad until you actually eat it. Season it with taco seasoning, let it cool completely before it goes in, and it turns this from a side dish into something you could serve as dinner on its own. That’s the part that catches people off guard.

Ingredients in Cowboy Pasta Salad

  • Rotini or cavatappi pasta (1 pound): Either works. Use whatever you have on hand.
  • Ground beef (1 pound): 85 to 90 percent lean. Cooked and seasoned with taco seasoning, then cooled before it goes into the salad.
  • Taco seasoning (1 tablespoon): Goes on the beef with a splash of water and simmers until it coats everything. Store bought works fine.
  • Thick cut bacon (8 ounces, chopped): Thick cut so it stays crispy in the salad instead of going limp. Cook it until it’s properly crisp.
  • Corn kernels (1½ cups): Charred in a dry skillet until blistered and browned. Canned or frozen both work, more on why this step matters below.
  • Cherry tomatoes (1½ cups, halved): Fresh, sweet, and exactly what this salad needs to balance the richness.
  • Sharp cheddar (1½ cups, cubed or shredded): Sharp is the one to reach for, mild cheddar gets lost in a dressing this bold.
  • Black beans (1 can, drained and rinsed): Bulk, protein, and that classic Tex Mex flavor.
  • Green onions (3, sliced) and jalapeño (1, seeded and minced): Onions bring freshness, jalapeño brings heat. Leave some seeds in if you want more kick.
  • Mayonnaise (1 cup) and sour cream (½ cup): The creamy base. Full fat for both, no substitutes here.
  • Barbecue sauce (3 tablespoons): Smoke and a little sweetness. Use your favorite brand.
  • Lime juice (2 tablespoons): Fresh squeezed. Brightens everything and keeps the dressing from feeling heavy.
  • Chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and hot sauce: The spice layer, this is where the whole thing comes together.

How to Make Cowboy Pasta Salad

Cook the pasta in well salted boiling water until just al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water until the pasta is completely cool. The cold rinse stops the cooking and washes off the surface starch so the salad stays loose and not gluey. Set aside.

While the pasta cooks, whisk all the dressing ingredients together in a bowl and refrigerate it. Letting it sit while you build the rest of the salad gives the flavors time to come together and the dressing will taste noticeably better for it.

Cook the chopped bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving a little of the fat behind in the pan. Add the ground beef to the same pan and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the taco seasoning and a splash of water and simmer for 2 minutes until the seasoning coats the beef. Set it aside to cool completely before it goes into the salad.

Now the corn. I just used the same skillet, maybe wipe some of that extra grease off and heat it over medium high with no additional oil. Add the corn and let it sit without stirring for a minute or two before tossing. You’re looking for dark blistered spots, not just warmed corn. This charring is where most of the smoky cookout flavor comes from and it takes about 5 minutes total. Don’t skip this step.

Combine the cooled pasta, beef, bacon, charred corn, cherry tomatoes, cheddar, black beans, green onions, and jalapeño in a large bowl. Pour the dressing over the top and toss until everything is well coated. Taste and adjust with more salt or hot sauce if needed.

Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to an hour. If it sits longer and absorbs the dressing, stir in a splash more mayo or sour cream before serving and it comes right back.

Tips and Tricks

  • Cool everything before tossing. Warm beef or warm pasta will wilt the tomatoes, melt the cheese, and make the dressing separate. Let everything cool properly before the salad comes together.
  • Refrigerate the dressing while you work. Even 20 minutes in the fridge gives the flavors time to meld and the dressing tastes better for it.
  • Char the corn properly. You want actual dark blistered spots, not just heated corn. High heat, no oil, patience.
  • Rinse the pasta. Always for a cold pasta salad. Always.
  • Make it ahead. This salad is excellent made a few hours ahead and refrigerated. Just hold back a little dressing and toss it in right before serving if it looks like it’s absorbed too much.
  • Taste and adjust at the end. The dressing is bold but the salad has a lot going on. Taste the finished salad and add more lime, hot sauce, or salt as needed.

Cowboy Pasta Salad

Prep 20 minutes minutes
Cook 20 minutes minutes
Total 40 minutes minutes
–+
Rate Recipe Print Recipe
Cowboy Pasta Salad with seasoned ground beef, crispy bacon, charred corn, black beans, sharp cheddar, and cherry tomatoes all tossed in a smoky barbecue mayo dressing with lime and chili powder. Feeds 10 people and gets better as it sits.

Ingredients

For the dressing

  • 1 cup mayonnaise
  • ½ cup sour cream
  • 3 tablespoons barbecue sauce
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice
  • 1 teaspoon chili powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  • Hot sauce (to taste)

For the salad

  • 1 pound rotini (or cavatappi pasta)
  • 1 pound ground beef
  • 1 tablespoon taco seasoning
  • 8 ounces thick cut bacon (chopped)
  • 1½ cups corn kernels
  • 1½ cups cherry tomatoes (halved)
  • 1½ cups sharp cheddar cheese (cubed or shredded)
  • 15 ounces black beans (1 can, drained and rinsed)
  • 3 green onions (sliced)
  • 1 jalapeño (seeded and minced)

Before You Begin! If you make this, please leave a review and rating letting us know how you liked this recipe! This helps our business thrive & continue providing free recipes.

Instructions 

  • Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the 1 pound pasta just until al dente. Drain, rinse under cold water to stop the cooking, and set aside. Rinsing matters here, it washes off the surface starch so the salad does not turn gluey.
  • While the pasta cooks, make the dressing. Whisk together the 1 cup mayonnaise, ½ cup sour cream, 3 tablespoons barbecue sauce, 2 tablespoons lime juice, 1 teaspoon chili powder, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, ½ teaspoon garlic powder, ½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, and a few dashes of hot sauce. Refrigerate it while you build the rest, so the flavors have time to come together.
  • Cook the 8 ounces chopped bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving a little of the fat in the pan.
  • Add the 1 pound ground beef to the same skillet and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the 1 tablespoon taco seasoning and a splash of water, then simmer for 2 minutes until it coats the beef. Set it aside to cool.
  • Char the 1½ cups corn in a dry skillet over medium high heat, tossing every couple of minutes, until browned and blistered in spots. This step is small but it is where a lot of the smoky, cookout flavor comes from, so do not skip it.
  • In a large bowl, combine the cooled pasta, browned beef, bacon, charred corn, 1½ cups cherry tomatoes, 1½ cups cheddar, the black beans, sliced green onions, and minced jalapeño. Pour the dressing over the top and toss until everything is well coated. Taste and adjust with more salt or hot sauce.
  • Serve right away, or chill for up to an hour. If it sits longer and drinks up the dressing, just stir in a splash more before serving.

Notes

  1. Cool everything before tossing: Warm beef or pasta will wilt the tomatoes, melt the cheese, and make the dressing separate. Let everything cool completely first.
  2. Rinse the pasta: Cold water rinse after draining stops the cooking and washes off surface starch that would make the salad gluey. Always rinse pasta for a cold salad.
  3. Char the corn properly: High heat, no oil, let it sit without stirring for a minute or two at a time. You want actual dark blistered spots not just warmed corn. This is where the smoky cookout flavor comes from.
  4. Refrigerate the dressing while you work: Even 20 minutes in the fridge lets the flavors meld. The dressing tastes noticeably better for it.
  5. Hold back some dressing: If making ahead reserve about a quarter of the dressing and toss it in right before serving if the salad has absorbed too much.
  6. Sharp cheddar: Mild cheddar gets lost in the bold dressing. Sharp cheddar has enough flavor to stand up to everything else going on.
  7. Thick cut bacon: Stays crispier in the salad than regular bacon. Worth seeking out.
  8. Jalapeño heat: Seeded and minced for mild heat. Leave some seeds in for more kick. Leave it out entirely for no heat.
  9. Make ahead: Excellent made a few hours ahead. Gets better as it sits. Just refresh with a little extra dressing before serving if needed.
  10. Storage: Up to 3 days in the fridge. Stir in extra mayo or sour cream before serving if it’s absorbed the dressing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make this ahead of time?

Yes and I’d actually encourage it. The flavors develop and meld as it sits. Make it a few hours ahead, hold back about a quarter of the dressing, and toss the reserved dressing in right before serving if the salad has absorbed too much.

Can I use a different pasta shape?

I’d use something with ridges or spirals that hold the dressing well. Rotini and cavatappi are my top choices. Penne or farfalle also work. I’d avoid smooth shapes like spaghetti or linguine that don’t grip the dressing.

Can I leave out the ground beef?

Yes. The salad is still excellent without it, just heartier with it. If you skip the beef I’d double the bacon to compensate.

How spicy is this?

Mildly spicy with 1 seeded jalapeño and a few dashes of hot sauce. Remove the jalapeño entirely for no heat or add more hot sauce and leave the jalapeño seeds in for more kick.

Can I use a different protein?

Yes. Shredded rotisserie chicken works beautifully here instead of or alongside the ground beef. Grilled steak strips would also be excellent.

How long does it keep?

Up to 3 days in the fridge covered tightly. Stir in a little extra mayo or sour cream before serving if it’s absorbed the dressing.
